**STEP 1 - Scene:** A plated main course: pieces of salmon fillet with a pale green herb crust or sauce, seen from directly above on a white square plate. Nothing else is on the plate.

**STEP 2 - Ruler:** The plate is a square-ish dinner plate about 26 cm across, so the area is about 530 cm².

**STEP 3 - Items:** (a) salmon fillet, pink flesh, in three pieces; (b) green herb crust or creamy herb sauce on top; (c) a few small herb leaves.

**STEP 4 - Area:** Salmon pieces cover about 20% of the plate (top piece ~12%, right piece ~4%, bottom-left piece ~4%). Herb crust covers the same areas, so it is included in those pieces. Leaves are negligible. Total food coverage is about 20%.

**STEP 5 - Volume:** Top piece ~64 cm² × 1.5 cm ≈ 96 ml; the other two pieces together ≈ 85 ml. Total gross volume ≈ 180 ml.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Salmon with crust at ~0.9 g/ml gives about 160 g. Splitting this into flesh (~150 g) and herb crust/sauce (~60 g) is a reasonable approximation for the plated weight. I've scaled the total to about 210 g to account for the sauce.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Cooked salmon ≈ 206 kcal/100 g, so 150 g ≈ 309 kcal. Herb crust/creamy sauce ≈ 150 kcal/100 g, so 60 g ≈ 90 kcal. Total ≈ 400 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** About 210 g of salmon with a herb crust, covering roughly a fifth of a dinner plate, is plausible. The estimate is a single portion of about 400 kcal.
